styles.name: mobius-strip
styles.description: A one-sided Möbius band with its half-twist, hidden lines removed, cross-rulings flowing round it as it slides along the bar

styles.name: torus-wireframe
styles.description: A doughnut torus in perspective, hidden-line wireframe spinning about its axis as it rolls along the bar

styles.name: torus-knot
styles.description: A five-lobed (2,5) torus knot with true over/under crossings, turning slowly as it slides along the bar

styles.name: trefoil-knot
styles.description: The three-lobed trefoil knot with alternating over/under crossings, rocking in 3-D as it slides along the bar

styles.name: klein-bottle
styles.description: A glass Klein bottle lying on its side: the neck bends back and passes through the wall (hidden lines dotted) as it turns and slides along

styles.name: hopf-fibers
styles.description: Three Hopf fibers — circles that each link every other — stereographically projected, interlocked with over/under crossings and turning

styles.name: sphere-inflate
styles.description: A spinning latitude/longitude globe, back half hidden, inflating from a pea to full size as it rolls along the bar

styles.name: helix-climb
styles.description: A DNA-style double helix screwing along the bar: two strands in opposite phase with base-pair rungs, the back strand broken where it passes behind

styles.name: saddle-surface
styles.description: Hyperbolic paraboloid z = x²−y² wireframe — the canonical saddle point, revealed as a grid of iso-lines, rotating with time

styles.name: tesseract-spin
styles.description: 4-D hypercube (tesseract) rotated in the XW and YZ planes then perspective-projected to 2-D — the full inner/outer cube wireframe turning inside out as it slides along the bar

styles.name: roman-surface
styles.description: Steiner's Roman surface — one of the most beautiful immersions of ℝP² into ℝ³, with six Whitney umbrella singularities, revealed petal by petal

styles.name: seifert-ramp
styles.description: Seifert-surface-inspired spiral ramp spanning a trefoil knot boundary — a twisted disk that rises through a full turn as progress advances
